newsitem.title: ITALY: EC's Van Miert sees 6-month delay on IRI debt deal.
newsitem.headline: EC's Van Miert sees 6-month delay on IRI debt deal.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday that Italy had asked for a one year extension on the terms of a 1993 agreement on reducing industrial holding IRI's debt, but said he believed only a six-month delay was possible.

"The government asked for an extension of one year, but I think that we cannot extend it for more than six months because we want to ensure that the privatisations are done quickly," Van Miert told a briefing at Rome's foreign press association.
Under the existing accord between Italy and the European Commission, IRI must cut its debt to below 5.0 trillion lire ($3.3 billion) by the end of 1996.

Van Miert said he would recommend to the commission to grant Italy a six-month extension. He had said last month that an extension would be needed because of hitches in Italy's privatisation programme that have delayed the sale of IRI-controlled telecoms holding Stet.

IRI's net debt at the end of 1995 was 22.456 trillion lire. Stet is slated for sale next February or March and the group will probably also have to sell-off its motorway toll group Autostrade SpA to meet the EC terms.
